mechanism_builds.causal_path: Subject-level covariates (age, BMI, medication, pathology) → induce non-identical conditional distributions of physiological signals across individuals → calibration set from one subject stratum fails to represent test subject stratum → exchangeability assumption violated → marginal coverage guarantee fails
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Increased inter-subject heterogeneity (measured by covariate distance) leads to decreased empirical coverage on test subjects relative to nominal level
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Calibration and test subjects differ in age >10 years, BMI >5 kg/m², or medication class
measurable_outcomes: Empirical coverage probability per subject stratum
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: The mechanism is strongest when calibration data lacks representation of test subject covariates; finite-sample exchangeability breaks when covariate shift exceeds a threshold quantifiable via Wasserstein distance between subject-level feature distributions.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Physiological state (activity) → increases motion artifacts and electrode impedance changes → induces heteroscedastic prediction errors (error variance correlates with signal quality) → standard conformal scores assume homoscedasticity → marginal quantile underestimates tail errors during high-artifact segments → conditional coverage drops during motion
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Higher accelerometer magnitude and lower signal quality index lead to larger prediction error variance and lower conditional coverage
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Motion artifact amplitude >20% of signal amplitude
Conformal score function does not condition on signal quality
measurable_outcomes: Conditional coverage given signal quality index bins
Prediction error variance as function of accelerometer magnitude
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Adaptive scores using real-time signal quality indices (e.g., normalized residuals by estimated noise standard deviation) can restore conditional coverage if noise model is well-calibrated.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Circadian/ultradian phase → modulates autonomic tone → shifts distribution of HRV, BP, RSA → prediction error distribution shifts with phase → calibration set from one phase (e.g., morning) non-exchangeable with test phase (e.g., nocturnal) → marginal coverage fails at phase transitions
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage decreases when calibration and test segments differ in circadian phase >π/2 radians (6 hours) or ultradian phase >π/2; coverage lowest during sleep-wake transitions
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Calibration data collected only during daytime
measurable_outcomes: Conditional coverage per circadian phase bin
Coverage at sleep-wake transitions vs. stable sleep
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Time-stratified calibration (e.g., separate quantiles per 4-hour block) or phase-aware scores (including time-of-day as feature) can mitigate if sufficient per-phase data exists.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Sparse asynchronous reference measurements → label noise correlated with clinical concern (e.g., cuff triggered by alarm) → nonconformity scores biased upward during high-concern states → empirical quantile overestimates typical error → intervals too wide during routine states, but label noise heteroscedasticity causes under-coverage during high-concern states if noise distribution skewed
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Higher label noise variance and stronger state-dependence (correlation between clinical_concern_flag and label noise) lead to larger bias in empirical quantile and worse conditional coverage
measurable_outcomes: Bias of empirical quantile vs. true quantile
Conditional coverage given clinical concern flag
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Modeling label noise as heteroscedastic (e.g., via replicate measurements) and using noise-aware nonconformity scores can reduce bias.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Disease state alters physiology (e.g., reduced HRV in HF) → increases prediction error variance for that subpopulation → marginal conformal averages over subpopulations → nominal coverage achieved overall but conditional coverage for high-risk subpopulation far below nominal → dangerous under-coverage for those needing it most
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Subpopulations with higher prediction error variance (e.g., HF, sepsis) have lower conditional coverage; severity of under-coverage correlates with disease severity score
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Prediction error variance ratio between subpopulations >2
measurable_outcomes: Conditional coverage per disease label (if known)
Interval width inflation needed to achieve group-conditional coverage
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Latent clustering of residuals (e.g., Gaussian mixture on residuals) can identify high-error regimes; group-conditional conformal on clusters can improve worst-case coverage.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Strong autocorrelation in physiological time series (phi >0.8) → reduces effective sample size n_eff = n * (1-phi)/(1+phi) → empirical quantile variance inflated by factor n/n_eff → finite-sample coverage guarantee (which assumes n_eff = n) becomes anti-conservative → actual coverage below nominal
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Higher autocorrelation (phi) leads to lower effective sample size, higher quantile variance, and lower empirical coverage for fixed nominal n
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Conformal method uses standard i.i.d. quantile
measurable_outcomes: Effective sample size estimated via autocorrelation
Empirical coverage vs. nominal across phi values
Quantile variance vs. theoretical i.i.d. variance
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Corrected quantile estimators using block bootstrap or autoregressive model-based effective sample size can restore coverage.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Physiological adaptation (medication titration, vascular remodeling) → gradual shift in P(Y|X) → prediction error distribution drifts → fixed calibration set becomes outdated → coverage degrades over time until recalibration → drift rate correlates with clinical trajectory (worsening patients drift faster)
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage decreases monotonically with days since calibration; slope of coverage decline steeper for patients with medication changes or worsening clinical scores
measurable_outcomes: Coverage as function of days since calibration
Drift detection delay using residual distribution tests
Coverage after drift-triggered recalibration vs. fixed schedule
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Drift-aware conformal using sequential tests on residuals (e.g., KS test, CUSUM) can trigger recalibration adaptively.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Clinical state (e.g., hypoperfusion) → causes modality dropout (PPG loss) → creates distinct error regime with higher prediction error → marginal conformal averages over regimes → overall coverage nominal but coverage during dropout near zero → critical failures when sensor loss indicates clinical deterioration
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage conditional on modality dropout (e.g., PPG missing) significantly lower than nominal; dropout probability correlates with clinical severity
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Conformal score does not include modality presence features
measurable_outcomes: Conditional coverage per active modality combination
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Modality-aware nonconformity scores (e.g., separate quantiles per modality subset) can maintain conditional coverage if dropout regimes are identifiable.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Physiological signal distribution skewed/heavy-tailed → absolute residual score produces symmetric intervals → intervals too narrow in heavy tail (under-coverage during extremes) and too wide in bulk (over-coverage) → coverage varies systematically with signal magnitude (e.g., hypertensive crisis under-covered)
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: For skewed signals, absolute residual score yields lower coverage in high-magnitude tail quantiles (e.g., top 10%) and higher coverage in central quantiles; distribution-aware scores (e.g., quantile regression) equalize conditional coverage across quantiles
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Nonconformity score not adapted to distribution
measurable_outcomes: Conditional coverage per decile of predicted value
Calibration of prediction intervals via PIT histogram
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Learned nonconformity scores (e.g., via quantile regression forests) can adapt to local scale and skewness but require sufficient data to avoid overfitting.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Clinical context (ICU vs. ward vs. home) confounds X→Y relationship (same tachycardia means different things) → context labels missing at deployment → conformal predictor averages over contexts → marginal coverage nominal but conditional coverage per context varies widely → dangerous under-coverage in high-stakes contexts (ICU)
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage conditional on ICU context lower than ward/home if calibration dominated by ward data; coverage gap increases with context confounder strength and missingness
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Calibration data from single context (e.g., only ward)
Outcome distribution differs significantly across contexts (e.g., BP mean shift >10 mmHg)
measurable_outcomes: Conditional coverage per context (if labels available)
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Context-invariant representation learning (e.g., domain adversarial training) combined with conformal prediction can recover stable coverage if context-invariant features exist.
